content.title: About
content.content: Canned Refried Beans (pinto) are a ready‑to‑eat product made from cooked pinto beans that are mashed, lightly fried with oil, and seasoned with salt and spices. The beans are sealed in airtight cans, giving them a long shelf life without refrigeration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pinto beans are one of the most popular bean varieties in Mexico and the United States.
The term “refried” comes from the Spanish “refrito,” meaning “fried again.”
Canned refried beans are commonly used as a base for burritos, tacos, chili, and side dishes.
Cans typically have a shelf life of 2 to 5 years thanks to sterile packaging.
Variants may be low‑salt or flavored with cumin, chili powder, or other spices.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Pinto beans provide about 7 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most of the fat comes from the added oil, making it suitable for moderate‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned versions often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands add preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Refried beans are ready to eat straight from the can: heat in the microwave or on the stove, add to tacos, burritos, chips, soups, or use as a filling for casseroles. Mix with cheese, avocado, or fresh herbs for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
